positioning_canvas.title: Map ICP and category maturity
positioning_canvas.prompt:
Fill only ICP Positioning and Category Positioning for [product] on [client board] in [market]. Confirm the active product, read its Product Architecture and existing positioning, and preserve unrelated work and other products. Research relevant official product sources; distinguish evidence from illustrative assumptions.

Map ICPs from the most primitive operating setup to mature setups for the department using this product, not the entire company. People = relevant roles and their counts; Process = how work is currently done; Technology = current tools and systems; Input = the workload or population served. For payroll, People means HR/payroll staff and Input means employee headcount served. Label staffing and size ranges as illustrative, not fixed benchmarks.

Within each ICP, treat these four columns as independent lists. Add as many rows as any column needs. A technology-only, people-only or process-only row is valid: leave other cells empty. Never invent, repeat or pad entries to fill every cell, and do not imply entries sharing a row necessarily correspond. State a shared input/headcount once; repeat only for a genuinely different input.

Map relevant category families from primitive substitutes to more integrated solutions, explaining which ICP setups they serve and how the operating model changes. Categories can overlap; do not force a headcount ladder or call every new feature/technology a new category. Distinguish software categories from manual substitutes and outsourced services; add verified illustrative providers where useful.

Leave ICP/category selection to the user unless explicitly directed. Do not fill Competitive Positioning or Value Positioning, sync competitors into Keywords, or change other sections. Save to this product's Positioning Canvas, preserving other products and current edits. Verify the saved ICP rows and categories; warn about stale open-board saves before an external update.

product_architecture.title: Build a product architecture
product_architecture.prompt:
Build the Product Architecture for [product] on [client board], using [product URL] and [target market, if known]. Read the existing architecture first and preserve existing work unless replacement is requested.

Research official product pages and documentation for this product and comparable software. Consolidate the relevant capabilities into a proposed software-module architecture. Distinguish native capabilities, external integrations and optional extensions; do not imply the product already supports every researched feature.

Create one adjustable row per workflow; the workflow itself is the process. Use only Technology and People nodes, with short, specific names. Show people only where someone supplies input, reviews or approves. Put input data and output names on connectors, not separate data or process nodes.

Arrange each workflow left to right. When one input feeds parallel technologies, stack those technologies vertically and group them under a common name. Connect their results to a shared destination or separate destinations as appropriate. Keep real dependencies in sequence, and connect related workflows. Leave enough space for readable nodes and connector labels.

Save to the Strategy Product Architecture workflow editor using product_architecture_set, not the older generic canvas. Attach a concise feature/source map to Grounded Evidences, distinguish researched facts from proposed design, and verify the saved nodes, groups and labelled connections.
